message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and ensure safe, habitable living conditions. Below is an overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (Texas Property Code, Chapter 24) and related statutes: | Category | Key Rights | Practical Implications | |----------|------------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | • Keep records of the unit’s condition at move‑in and move‑out. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control.
• Must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary condition. | • Report problems promptly; landlords must respond within a reasonable time. | | **Repair & Deduct / Rent Withhold** | • If landlord fails to repair, tenant may pay for repairs and deduct cost from rent, or withhold rent until repairs are made. | • Keep receipts and document the issue. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot disturb the tenant’s peaceful use of the property. | • Unreasonable entry or harassment is prohibited. | | **Entry Notice** | • Landlord must give 24‑hour written notice before entering, except in emergencies. | • Document any unannounced entries. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing if it lasts longer than one year.
• Must include rent amount, security deposit, and lease duration. | • Verify all terms are spelled out. | | **Rent Increases** | • No limit on how much rent can be increased, but must be in writing and not exceed the amount stated in the lease. | • Review lease for any rent‑increase clauses. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | • File complaints with the Texas Commission on Human Rights if discrimination occurs. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must provide written notice (30 days for nonpayment, 60 days for lease violations).
• Eviction requires a court order; unlawful detainer actions are governed by Texas Property Code § 24.602. | • Respond to notices promptly; seek legal counsel if facing eviction. | | **Right to Repair** | • If landlord fails to fix major issues, tenant may sue for damages or terminate the lease. | • Keep a log of maintenance requests. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide hot water, heating, and electricity unless otherwise specified. | • Verify utility responsibilities in the lease. | | **Subletting** | • Tenant may sublet only with landlord’s written consent, which cannot be unreasonably withheld. | • Obtain written permission before subletting. | | **Insurance** | • Landlord is not required to insure the unit; tenant may obtain renter’s insurance. | • Consider renter’s insurance for personal belongings. | | **Legal Remedies** | • Tenants can file a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office or the local housing authority. | • Seek legal aid if needed. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Take photos, keep copies of all correspondence, and record dates of any maintenance requests or disputes. 2. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with the Texas Property Code, especially Chapters 24 (Residential Landlord‑Tenant Law) and 24.602 (Unlawful Detainer). 3. **Use Written Notices** – When you receive a notice from your landlord, respond in writing and keep copies. 4. **Seek Legal Assistance** – If you’re unsure about your rights or face potential eviction, consult a tenant‑rights organization or a lawyer specializing in landlord‑tenant law. ### Resources - **Texas Property Code** – Chapter 24 (https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/PR/htm/PR.24.htm) - **Texas Commission on Human Rights** – Discrimination complaints (https://www.tchra.org/) - **Texas Attorney General – Housing** – Consumer protection (https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/) - **Local Housing Authorities** – For eviction assistance and tenant support. If you have a specific situation (e.g., a notice of eviction, a maintenance dispute, or a lease clause you’re unsure about), let me know and I can help you draft a letter or outline next steps.
